sections.content: How many people stayed in North Hykeham after gaining qualifications?

North Hykeham is a small town in the East Midlands. North Hykeham does not have its own university.

North Hykeham has lower levels of deprivation.

Overall, North Hykeham ended up with:

  • more graduates than it produced
  • more non-graduates with advanced qualifications than it produced
Note: all towns and cities in this analysis are defined based on population size only. This means that some cities are classed as towns because of their population.

Let's explore this further

There were 695 state-school pupils from North Hykeham who sat their GCSEs between the 2007 to 2008 and the 2010 to 2011 school years.

Of these, 205 (29%) went on to gain degree-level qualifications (level 6+ as defined by The Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation, or Ofqual ). We will call these people graduates.

Another 215 (31%) went on to gain other advanced post-16 qualifications, such as A-Levels, a foundation degree or higher apprenticeship (levels 3-5 as defined by Ofqual). In this tool, we will refer to these non-graduates with advanced qualifications as “qualified non-graduates", for brevity.

The charts below compare North Hykeham to other English towns and cities using three measures:

  • what proportion of North Hykeham's pupils became graduates or qualified non-graduates by the 2017 to 2018 academic year
  • of those graduates and qualified non-graduates, the percentages that lived in North Hykeham in the 2018 to 2019 academic year
  • how many graduates and qualified non-graduates from elsewhere came to live there by 2018 to 2019, relative to the number who sat their GCSEs there

In some towns, some of this information may not be available because of small sample sizes.
The size and deprivation level of a town, as well as the qualification levels of older residents, were all related to students' educational attainment. Read our previous analysis.

Where did those who left North Hykeham move to?

Of North Hykeham's graduates, 115 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 45 of those graduates (39%) were living fairly locally, in the Lincoln travel to work area (TTWA).

Of North Hykeham's qualified (level 3+) non-graduates, 100 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 75 of those qualified non-graduates (75%) were living fairly locally, in the Lincoln travel to work area (TTWA).

Of those in North Hykeham's GCSE cohort:

  • 65 graduates left the East Midlands

In 2018 to 2019, 67% of graduates and 56% of qualified non-graduates living in North Hykeham had moved there from elsewhere

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, there were 260 graduates and 250 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates from our cohort living in North Hykeham. This is compared with the 205 graduates and 215 qualified non-graduates who had lived there when they sat their GCSEs.

In 2018 to 2019, 33% of the graduates had also lived in North Hykeham as GCSE pupils, while 67% had moved there from elsewhere.

Of the qualified non-graduates who lived in North Hykeham in 2018 to 2019, 46% had lived there as GCSE pupils, while 56% had moved to the area from elsewhere.
